question: Does forcing a learned visual world model to preserve 2D sensory topology through local recurrent convolution—and modulating designated spatial channels with motor commands—yield smoother physical prediction, better policy optimization through a frozen model, and body-linked representations than an unstructured latent-vector world model?

key_findings.claim: The proposed world model is a finite Amari-style spatial recurrent map whose local kernel and motor-gated channels make physical prediction geometrically explicit.
key_findings.evidence: Each hidden channel is a complete 2D map. The update is h_(t+1)=h_t+(delta t/tau)[-h_t+K*ReLU(h_t)+W_in*I_t], where learned K is a local 7x7 convolution; a 1x1 output convolution reconstructs pixels. Visual input is present only for the first three frames, after which the field rolls out autonomously. In the arm task, the first four of 32 channels are assigned one-to-one to shoulder/elbow co-contraction and reciprocal commands and multiplied by the corresponding scalar motor signals after each dynamics update. The ballistic task uses 16 channels and no motor gating.

anchors.section: Neural Field Architecture, Equations 1-2 and Figure 1

key_findings.claim: On the simple ballistic environment, the neural field reports lower pixel prediction error and smoother blind trajectories than the VAE-LSTM baseline across ten seeds.
key_findings.evidence: After three observed frames, the 32x32 model predicts the remaining ball trajectory. Median MSE is 9.33e-4 with IQR [8.95e-4, 9.88e-4], versus VAE-LSTM median 3.94e-3 (p<0.001). Maximum predicted-centroid displacement is 2.06 pixels versus 21.97, and 0.0% versus 15.4% of blind-rollout sequences contain a jump above three pixels (p<0.001). The field uses about 13K parameters versus 850K for this baseline.

anchors.section: Experiment 1 Physics from Lateral Dynamics; Figure 2

key_findings.claim: The zero-teleportation result is partly an enforced architectural bound, not independent evidence that the model discovered continuous physical motion.
key_findings.evidence: The teleport criterion is a frame-to-frame centroid jump greater than three pixels, while the 7x7 local kernel has a spatial radius of three and the authors explicitly state that locality bounds one-step displacement. Thus the neural field's 0% teleportation is an expected consequence of constraining signal propagation. Its lower MSE and approximately parabolic rollouts add empirical content, but the discontinuity metric itself favors the design by construction and is not evaluated against a parameter-matched convolutional recurrent baseline with the same locality.

anchors.section: Discussion, locality constrains errors to smooth spatial drift

key_findings.claim: A policy optimized through the frozen neural-field simulator transfers much better to the underlying planar-arm physics environment than a policy optimized through the VAE-LSTM.
key_findings.evidence: The world model first learns from random motor-babbling trajectories. A CNN+LSTM catch surrogate is then trained on reconstructed trajectories paired with ground-truth catch/miss labels, both modules are frozen, and gradients through long imagined rollouts update only the policy. Over 100 evaluation episodes, the neural-field policy catches 81.5% (IQR [79.2%,84.7%]), versus 46.0% for VAE-LSTM policies (p=0.003) and 89.0% for policies trained directly on the target physics. This is learned-model-to-ground-truth-simulator transfer in a 2D computational environment, not deployment on a physical robot.

anchors.section: Training and Evaluation; Experiment 2 Frozen-Simulator Policy Learning

key_findings.claim: The policy-learning stage is offline with respect to the target physics, but the complete method is not environment-free because both learned components receive prior ground-truth-physics data.
key_findings.evidence: The neural field is trained on motor-babbling trajectories from the target environment. The catch predictor receives per-timestep catch/miss labels from corresponding real-physics rollouts while consuming world-model reconstructions. Only after those stages are the world model and catch predictor frozen and the policy updated without further target interaction. The result therefore supports reusing a previously learned differentiable simulator for a new policy objective, not learning control from wholly offline sensory prediction without task-labeled environment experience.

anchors.section: Training and Evaluation, three-stage frozen-simulator protocol
Experiment 2 policy optimization through fixed modules
Discussion, Grush's emulation theory and training order

key_findings.claim: Comparable arm-task pixel loss does not imply comparable control transfer, providing the paper's strongest evidence that rollout structure matters beyond one-step reconstruction fit.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 5 reports comparable final arm-task MSE for neural field and VAE-LSTM, and Figure 4 says their simulator-training catch-predictor values are also comparable, yet target-physics catch rates are 81.5% versus 46.0%. This dissociation is consistent with coherent gradients through spatial rollouts aiding policy transfer. It remains an architecture-package comparison, because parameter count, representation, recurrence, training procedure, and optimization stability all differ and no continuity-matched ablation is run.

key_findings.claim: Only reciprocal motor channels show the reported post hoc arm selectivity; co-contraction channels are explicit negative results.
key_findings.evidence: The selectivity index is (motor-gated activity over arm / motor-gated activity over ball) divided by the same arm/ball ratio in the reconstruction, so values above one indicate excess arm localization. Median selectivity is 2.18 for shoulder reciprocal and 1.50 for elbow reciprocal, both p=0.002. Shoulder and elbow co-contraction channels are not significant (p=0.16 and p=0.96). The authors plausibly relate the difference to reciprocal commands producing visible motion while co-contraction mainly changes stiffness.

anchors.section: Training and Evaluation, body-schema selectivity index

key_findings.claim: The body-schema interpretation is conditional and substantially architected: channel identities are motor-supervised even though pixel-level body labels are absent.
key_findings.evidence: Four channels are explicitly designated and gated by named shoulder/elbow commands, and arm/ball masks are applied after training to compute selectivity. What emerges without pixel labels is spatial localization of action-linked activity, not discovery of which channels correspond to which effectors. The paper itself concedes the apparent circularity and narrows the claim: when motor-gated neural fields achieve visuomotor prediction, body-selective encoding follows. No ungated, shuffled-command, randomly gated, or globally gated control tests necessity of the one-command/one-channel assignment.

anchors.section: Implications, circularity objection and conditional claim

key_findings.claim: The VAE-LSTM comparison cannot identify locality, isomorphism, Amari dynamics, or motor gating as the unique cause of the gains.
key_findings.evidence: The paper explicitly says the benchmark is not parameter matched: neural fields use 13K versus 850K parameters for ballistics and 50K versus 1.7M for the arm, while VAE-LSTM training is staged for 10,000 VAE epochs plus 10,000 frozen-VAE/LSTM epochs because joint gradients destabilize it. The neural field is trained end-to-end for 10,000 epochs. ConvLSTM, S2RM, PhyDNet, spatial cellular automata, neural operators, and global-kernel or shuffled-topology variants are absent. A weaker and unstable unstructured baseline establishes feasibility, not which structural component is necessary.

anchors.section: Discussion, representational-format comparison and ConvLSTM caveat
Limitations and future directions, broader spatial model class

key_findings.claim: The historical claim that neural fields had not been explored as world models for planning and control is contradicted by direct primary-source predecessors.
key_findings.evidence: The introduction states that neural fields had not been explored as world models for planning/control. However, Marc Toussaint's arXiv:nlin/0306015 (2003) is titled 'Learning a world model and planning with a self-organizing, dynamic neural system' and its official abstract describes learned perception-action relations, lateral-connectivity transition knowledge, motor modulation, local mechanisms, and dynamic-field planning. Xue et al.'s arXiv:2311.00802 (CoRL 2023) likewise uses a fully convolutional density-field dynamics model, spatial locality, differentiable action rendering, and gradient-based trajectory optimization in simulation and real experiments. Neither is cited. The paper's specific architecture/evaluations can still be novel, but the broad first-use premise is false.

anchors.section: Introduction, neural fields as planning/control world models

key_findings.claim: The neuroscience interpretation is explicitly structural and preliminary, not evidence that cortex implements the learned model or training rule.
key_findings.evidence: The model preserves retinotopic maps, local lateral connectivity, and gain-like motor modulation, but uses backpropagation and does not fit neural recordings, human behavior, developmental time courses, or anatomical kernels. The paper calls the comparison structural, treats learning separately from architecture, and labels the three results preliminary. Its analogies to MT simulation, posterior-parietal gain fields, mental practice, dreams, agency comparators, and enactivism are hypotheses generated by the model rather than tested neuroscientific findings.

method.core_idea: Make a visual world model isomorphic to the represented 2D sensory field: preserve every hidden channel as a spatial map, restrict state propagation to a learned local convolution, and inject continuous motor commands by multiplicatively gating designated spatial channels. Then reuse the frozen differentiable model for policy optimization and inspect whether action-linked channels localize to the controlled body.
method.mechanism: A learned 7x7 kernel implements Amari-style lateral recurrence with decay, ReLU activity, and 1x1 visual input/output projections. The model sees three frames and then predicts blind; motor commands continue throughout arm rollouts. Ballistics use 16 ungated maps on 32x32 images. The planar double-pendulum arm uses 32 maps on a 120x45 field, with four maps gated by shoulder/elbow co-contraction/reciprocal scalars. Models train for 10,000 epochs with Adam and pixel MSE. For control, a model learned from random motor babbling and a CNN+LSTM catch surrogate trained from target-physics labels are frozen; gradients through their long rollouts train only a CNN+LSTM policy, which is then evaluated for 100 episodes in the target physics. A post hoc normalized arm-versus-ball activity ratio measures selectivity. The sole learned baseline is a 32-dimensional convolutional-VAE plus LSTM trained in two 10,000-epoch stages.
assumptions: The image plane is the relevant physical coordinate system, so local visual adjacency corresponds to local causal interaction and motion.
A 7x7 translation-equivariant kernel has enough receptive-field growth and dynamics to represent gravity, articulated-arm motion, and ball trajectories without object slots.
Three observed frames are sufficient to infer velocity and other state needed for long blind prediction.
Pixel MSE can train recurrent dynamics whose long-horizon gradients are useful for control despite compounding blur and uncertainty.
Multiplying one predesignated channel by each raw motor command is an adequate abstraction of cortical gain modulation and action conditioning.
A body-linked representation should be more active over arm pixels than ball pixels after normalizing by reconstruction activity.
The CNN+LSTM catch predictor accurately maps reconstructed trajectories to target catch outcomes and supplies policy gradients that remain meaningful far from its training rollouts.
The target physics used for data, labels, and final evaluation is close enough to the learned model that policy optimization does not exploit simulator errors.
The staged, much larger VAE-LSTM is a sufficient representative of latent-vector world models even though modern latent models and spatial recurrent models differ.
Ten-seed ballistic summaries and unreported seed counts for later statistics are sufficient to characterize robustness; the statistical test and multiplicity corrections are unspecified.
Smooth local centroid motion is a meaningful physical-quality criterion rather than only a direct consequence of the local kernel's receptive field.
Performance on one ballistic and one 2D catching environment can inform broader claims about intuitive physics, offline learning, and body schema.

techniques.role: Maintains a recurrent 2D activity map with decay and learned local lateral interactions instead of compressing each frame to an unstructured vector.
Forces the model to infer motion from a short observation window and then expose autonomous long-horizon dynamics.
Multiplies four designated maps by shoulder/elbow commands to couple action and predicted visual change through gain-like modulation.
Backpropagates a catch objective through a fixed world model and fixed outcome surrogate to update only a new policy.
Measures maximum frame-to-frame predicted-object displacement and the fraction of blind rollouts exceeding a three-pixel jump.
Divides motor-channel arm/ball activity by reconstruction arm/ball activity to detect localization beyond simple pixel prevalence.
Provides the paper's intended contrast between spatially isomorphic recurrence and globally mixed compressed latent dynamics.
Upper reference trains the catching policy directly in the target physics rather than through a learned simulator.

limitations: Author-stated: the demonstrations are simple 2D environments. Occlusion, collision, support, independent objects, and interaction may require layered object representations and learned coupling.
Author-stated: pixel-space isomorphism is not appropriate for full 3D physics; a volumetric physical-coordinate field would be needed to handle projective distortion and depth.

Author-stated: the VAE-LSTM is a representational-format contrast, not an exhaustive or parameter-matched world-model benchmark; ConvLSTM and other spatially structured alternatives may share the same benefits.
Author-stated: the cortical comparison is structural. The architecture uses backpropagation and does not claim that cortical learning follows the implemented optimizer.
Author-stated: body-selective encoding is conditional on successful motor-gated visuomotor prediction; motor gating and locality do not guarantee it.
Author-stated: the proposed architecture addresses fast automatic physical simulation for perception/action, not symbolic physical reasoning.

Reviewer-identified: no ablation removes locality, widens K to global connectivity, shuffles spatial positions, replaces multiplication with concatenation, removes motor gating, or varies the number/identity of gated channels. The three claimed constraints are never causally separated.

Reviewer-identified: the sole VAE-LSTM has 17-67x more parameters, a different 32D bottleneck, and a staged training procedure adopted because joint training is unstable. Its weakness cannot establish superiority over modern latent or spatial world models.

Reviewer-identified: key reproducibility details are absent: trajectory counts and splits, rollout horizons, Adam learning rate/batch size, delta t and tau, data ranges, model/policy layer sizes, seed count for Experiments 2-3, and statistical test definitions.

Reviewer-identified: the offline-policy pipeline has already used target-physics motor-babbling trajectories and target catch/miss labels to train the world model and outcome surrogate; only the final policy optimization stage avoids interaction.

Reviewer-identified: target evaluation is a simulated planar double pendulum, not a hardware or naturalistic sim-to-real experiment. Language such as 'real physics' and 'transfer to reality' can overstate the domain gap.

Reviewer-identified: body-channel identities are manually linked to named motor commands, and body/ball segmentation is used at analysis time. The model learns localization without pixel labels but does not discover the effector decomposition from scratch.

Reviewer-identified: four p-values are reported without test names, sample counts for later experiments, effect uncertainty for baselines, or multiple-comparison correction; only ballistic explicitly states ten seeds.

Reviewer-identified: the teleport threshold matches the three-pixel radius of the 7x7 kernel, making 0% teleportation partly guaranteed. A local ConvLSTM or equivalent same-receptive-field control is necessary.

Reviewer-identified: no stochastic dynamics, multimodal futures, observation noise, occlusion, distractors, distribution shift, changed gravity/body parameters, or held-out action regimes test robustness.
Reviewer-identified: the historical statement that neural fields had not been used as planning/control world models overlooks at least Toussaint 2003 and the 2023 Neural Field Dynamics model.
failure_modes: A strictly local 7x7 field cannot model instantaneous long-range effects, rigid constraints, teleportation that is physically valid in the domain, or contacts whose causal graph is not local in image coordinates.
Occlusion and overlapping objects can collapse distinct entities into one pixel-space activity pattern; local recurrence has no object permanence or identity mechanism.
Camera movement, perspective, depth, and 3D projection can make adjacent physical states non-adjacent in pixels and distant physical objects adjacent in the image.
Pixel MSE encourages blur under uncertain or multimodal futures, which can produce smooth but behaviorally wrong trajectories that still satisfy the no-teleport criterion.
Multiplicative raw motor commands can suppress or sign-flip designated maps; unseen command magnitudes or actuator coupling may push recurrent activity outside the training regime.
Policy gradients through long learned rollouts can exploit systematic simulator or catch-predictor errors, even when average pixel MSE is low.

A catch surrogate trained on motor-babbling trajectories may be unreliable on policies optimized to maximize it, creating model/surrogate exploitation that 100 evaluation episodes may not fully reveal.
The body selectivity ratio can be unstable when motor or reconstruction activity over the ball is small, and it does not measure causal necessity of the channel for control.
Co-contraction channels are explicit negative cases: commands that alter stiffness without visible motion do not develop the claimed body localization.
The VAE-LSTM's staged instability and teleportation may be artifacts of that baseline implementation; a convolutional recurrent or stochastic latent comparator may remove the gap.
Locality can ensure smooth errors while preventing rapid correction after an early position/velocity mistake, causing coherent but increasingly displaced blind rollouts.
A field trained in one fixed gravity, camera, arm geometry, and ball distribution may encode those constants rather than transferable intuitive physics.
reusable_insights: Evaluate world models with rollout properties tied to downstream use, not only pixel MSE; two models with comparable reconstruction loss can yield very different policy gradients and transfer.
Architectural locality supplies a hard regularizer against discontinuous state motion, which can be valuable when smooth propagation is known to be physically valid.
Freeze the learned simulator and task surrogate before policy learning to test whether a reusable model supports a genuinely new optimization stage.
Distinguish no-interaction policy optimization from an environment-free pipeline by itemizing where world-model data and task labels came from.
Normalize representation selectivity by the output reconstruction's spatial occupancy so a larger body region alone does not create apparent selectivity.
Retain negative sensorimotor channels: reciprocal versus co-contraction differences make the interpretation conditional on visibly action-coupled dynamics.
Use a direct target-physics-trained policy as an attainable upper reference alongside a learned-simulator alternative.
When an architectural constraint guarantees a diagnostic, add a matched model with the same constraint and measure prediction accuracy beyond that diagnostic.
Preserve explicit spatial maps when interpretability requires reading predicted location directly, but compare with other spatial recurrent families before attributing the effect to one formalism.
Separate architecture-level biological analogies from learning-rule claims and empirical neural fit; structural plausibility alone is hypothesis generation.
open_questions: Does the catching advantage survive a parameter- and compute-matched ConvLSTM, S2RM, PhyDNet, neural cellular automaton, or spatial RSSM baseline?
Which ingredient is necessary: local K, spatially aligned hidden maps, recurrence, multiplicative motor gating, end-to-end training, or smaller parameter count?
How do results change with kernel radius, dilations, global/shuffled connections, learned sparse topology, and explicit object layers?
Can the model handle collisions, occlusion, support relations, multiple independently moving objects, and stochastic outcomes?
Do policies transfer across changed gravity, camera pose, arm length/mass, actuator noise, ball speed, and out-of-distribution commands?
What are the exact dataset sizes, rollout horizons, optimizer settings, seed counts, test statistics, and per-seed results?
Can a policy exploit the frozen world model or catch surrogate, and how does uncertainty-aware or adversarial policy validation change the 81.5% result?
Does body selectivity persist under shuffled motor-channel assignments, ungated channels, command concatenation, or motor signals that control external tools rather than the body?
Are reciprocal-channel activations causally required for accurate arm prediction or catching, as tested by channel ablation/intervention?
Can neural activity or behavioral data distinguish this Amari-field mechanism from alternative spatial recurrent world models?
Would a 3D physical-coordinate field preserve isomorphism under perspective projection, and how would visual observations be inferred into it?
Can local biologically plausible learning rules train the same architecture and retain its prediction/control results?
How does the method compare historically and empirically with Toussaint's motor-modulated dynamic-field planner and Xue et al.'s differentiable Neural Field Dynamics model?

competitive_landscape.title: Learning a world model and planning with a self-organizing, dynamic neural system
competitive_landscape.relationship: Uncited, exceptionally direct historical predecessor to the claimed neural-field world-model/planning concept.
competitive_landscape.difference: Toussaint learns perception-action relations in a growing self-organizing layer, encodes transitions in lateral connectivity, modulates that connectivity with motor signals, and uses a dynamic field for planning with local Hebbian mechanisms. Neural Fields as World Models instead learns a fixed-grid Amari-style convolutional predictor by backpropagation from raw visual frames, freezes it for gradient policy optimization, and analyzes motor-channel body selectivity. The newer bundle and experiments differ, but the 2003 record directly contradicts the claim that neural fields had not been explored as world models for planning/control.

competitive_landscape.title: Convolutional LSTM Network: A Machine Learning Approach for Precipitation Nowcasting
competitive_landscape.relationship: Canonical spatial recurrent predictor and the most important missing locality-matched architecture baseline.
competitive_landscape.difference: ConvLSTM replaces fully connected input/state transitions with learned convolutions so recurrent memory preserves spatial structure, and it outperforms FC-LSTM on spatiotemporal forecasting. The target uses a simpler continuous-time-inspired field update with one local lateral kernel and explicit motor multiplication. A ConvLSTM arm/ball control comparison would test whether Amari dynamics and motor gating add value beyond the well-established spatial-recurrence principle.

competitive_landscape.title: Deep Visual Foresight for Planning Robot Motion
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct action-conditioned visual prediction and planning competitor from unlabeled interaction data.
competitive_landscape.difference: Finn and Levine combine an action-conditioned video predictor with model-predictive control and validate on a physical robot pushing novel objects, without calibrated sensing. The target instead optimizes a policy by analytic gradients through a frozen local neural field and evaluates in a simulated planar arm. It contributes stronger internal spatial interpretability and a body-channel analysis, but has a much narrower control domain and no hardware evidence.

competitive_landscape.title: World Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct latent-vector world-model predecessor and source of the target's VAE-LSTM baseline format and dream-policy motivation.
competitive_landscape.difference: Ha and Schmidhuber compress images with a VAE, model latent dynamics with an MDN-RNN, and train compact controllers, including entirely inside hallucinated environments before transfer. The target deliberately rejects unstructured latent geometry for a local 2D field and trains policies through differentiable trajectories instead of controller evolution. Its one VAE-LSTM implementation is not a full reproduction of the stochastic World Models system.

competitive_landscape.title: S2RMs: Spatially Structured Recurrent Modules
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct spatially structured recurrent world-model alternative omitted from the baseline panel.
competitive_landscape.difference: S2RMs model a dynamical system as sparsely interacting recurrent subsystems with learned topology informed by spatial locations, evaluating cropped-video prediction and partially observed StarCraft II world modeling with OOD task generalization. The target fixes topology to a regular 2D local kernel and adds motor gain channels, yielding easier spatial readout but less flexibility for nonlocal or modular interactions. S2RMs demonstrates that spatial world-model structure predates the target outside the Amari-field framing.

competitive_landscape.title: Disentangling Physical Dynamics from Unknown Factors for Unsupervised Video Prediction
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct physics-structured convolutional recurrent video-prediction competitor.
competitive_landscape.difference: PhyDNet separates a PDE-constrained PhyCell from a complementary ConvLSTM-like residual branch and evaluates four datasets with explicit ablations, missing-data tests, and long-term forecasting. The target learns an unconstrained local Amari kernel end to end and adds action gating/control/body analysis. PhyDNet supplies a much stronger prediction benchmark and component isolation; the target supplies a simpler interpretable field and downstream differentiable-policy test.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Field Dynamics Model for Granular Object Piles Manipulation
competitive_landscape.relationship: Uncited direct field-based, local, differentiable dynamics-and-planning predecessor.
competitive_landscape.difference: Xue et al. represent granular piles and pushers as Eulerian density fields, learn fully convolutional local dynamics, differentiably render actions, and optimize manipulation trajectories, with simulation, physical experiments, obstacle tasks, and zero-shot generalization. The target uses an Amari neural-activity field rather than a density field and uniquely studies cognitive analogies and body-channel selectivity, but its broad locality-plus-action-plus-gradient-planning premise and empirical scope are not first.

competitive_landscape.title: Mastering Diverse Domains through World Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Current strong latent world-model control competitor establishing modern breadth and robustness expectations.
competitive_landscape.difference: DreamerV3 learns a compact stochastic world model and actor/critic through imagined futures with one configuration across more than 150 tasks, including Minecraft from pixels and sparse rewards. The target sacrifices broad-domain performance and abstraction for an explicitly spatial, tiny, interpretable field and a controlled cognitive hypothesis. Without a Dreamer-style baseline, the target cannot argue spatial isomorphism is generally better for control; it only shows a gap against its VAE-LSTM in one planar task.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The author proposes 'isomorphic world models' that preserve sensory topology and presents motor-gated neural fields as a previously unexplored world-model substrate for physical prediction, offline task learning, and emergent body-linked representation. The same architecture is claimed to unite these capacities through action-conditional prediction in a spatial map.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The seven-page study supplies three linked experiments: ten-seed ballistic MSE/continuity, a three-stage frozen-simulator policy test with an 81.5% versus 46.0% catch-rate gap, and reciprocal-channel selectivity of 2.18/1.50 with nonsignificant co-contraction controls. The method is compact, interpretable, and uses the same local recurrence/motor-gating principle across prediction, control, and representation. The pixel-loss/control-transfer dissociation is particularly useful preliminary evidence.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The novel contribution is the specific combination of learned Amari-style visual fields, one-command/one-map multiplicative gating, frozen differentiable catching-policy optimization, and post hoc body-selectivity analysis in a cognitive-modeling argument. The broad historical premise is not novel: Toussaint 2003 already combines a learned world model, lateral connectivity, motor modulation, dynamic fields, and planning; ConvLSTM/S2RMs/PhyDNet preserve spatial recurrent structure; Xue et al. 2023 combine field dynamics, actions, and gradient planning. With one unmatched baseline and no component ablations, the results are promising preliminary demonstrations rather than evidence that isomorphism is the shared computational substrate of intuitive physics, mental practice, and body schema.

reviewer_notes: Secondary verification read every page of the seven-page arXiv v2/CogSci 2026 paper, including the complete discussion, limitations, acknowledgments, and references, and cross-checked all six PDF figures, equations, page mapping, and embedded v2 metadata. The review distinguishes target-physics simulation from hardware reality; policy-only offline learning from an environment-free pipeline; architectural smoothness from learned physical accuracy; and action-channel spatial localization from discovery of a body schema. Negative results retained co-contraction p=0.16/0.96, comparable arm MSE despite transfer differences, and acknowledged VAE-LSTM instability. Eight canonical competitor records were opened and version-pinned; the uncited 2003 and 2023 field/planning records materially narrow novelty. Confidence is limited by the short paper's missing implementation/statistical details, single unmatched baseline, absence of ablations, and broad cognitive interpretation.
